title: Glorify God by your life…… that was Dolly Parton’s mission
prayer: Lord, open my eyes to the ways You have always been present in my life. Take the gifts You have given me and the time still before me. Teach me to live them with joy and for Your glory. Above all, draw me nearer to You, until Your light becomes visible through mine. Amen.
body:
There is something difficult in today’s Gospel. Jesus stands among people who have known Him for years, yet they cannot recognize what God is doing right before them. Then He speaks of the widow of Zarephath and Naaman the Syrian—outsiders whom God chose to receive His grace. It angered them because God was not acting according to their expectations.

Perhaps that is what stayed with me: God’s presence and purpose do not always appear where, or how, we expect them to.

Last night I was reading about Dolly Parton and was touched by something she has often expressed—that her gifts came from God and were meant to be used for His glory. There was something about that simple recognition, and the joy with which she seems to live it, that made me reflect upon my own life.

Not whether I have done as much, but whether I have truly recognized God in what I have been given.

There comes a time when we begin to look differently at the years behind us and more carefully at the years still ahead. I know I have been given gifts. I know I have tried to use them, sometimes graciously and sometimes imperfectly. But now the desire feels different. I don’t want merely to use what God has given me. I want my life to belong to Him.

Maybe that is part of what this Gospel asks of us—to stop deciding beforehand where God should be found and begin noticing where He already is. Perhaps He has been present in our gifts, our ordinary encounters, our disappointments, even in the restless longing that tells us there must be something more.

And perhaps that longing itself is grace.

I cannot change the years already lived. But I can ask that whatever time remains becomes more conscious of Him, more available to Him, and somehow more capable of carrying His light.
